title: GR Recovery in Energy-Flow Cosmology via Density Saturation: Quantitative PPN Analysis for the Solar System
description: Derives the Solar System post-Newtonian limit of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) and shows that the modified Einstein equation acts as a scalar rescaling of GN, yielding Φ = Ψ and thus γ = 1 at linear order. Introduces a precise effective-density definition for the density saturation gate and demonstrates that dual screening (acceleration- and density-based) suppresses EFC modifications by 4–8 orders of magnitude below the Cassini bound.

author.name: Morten Magnusson
author.affiliation: Energy-Flow Cosmology Project | Symbiose Research Infrastructure

modified_einstein_equation.description: EFC field equation: a scalar rescaling of Newton's constant by a function of the entropy field S (modulated by density screening), which couples uniformly to the full stress-energy tensor.

density_saturation.description: Density-based screening gate that suppresses EFC modifications in high effective-density environments and activates them in low-density regimes.

effective_density.description: Mean enclosed density that sources the local Newtonian potential; identified as the physically relevant density entering the screening function.

acceleration_screening.description: Acceleration-based screening calibrated on galactic data (SPARC), driving EFC enhancements when local baryonic acceleration is low compared to the transition acceleration g†.

modified_poisson_phi.description: Linearized 00-component in Newtonian gauge: the same scalar rescaling multiplies the matter source in the Poisson equation for Φ.

modified_poisson_psi.description: Linearized spatial-trace equation: identical sourcing for Ψ implies no induced anisotropic stress at 1PN order and hence γ ≡ Ψ/Φ = 1.

key_results.main_finding: EFC yields γ = 1 exactly at linear order (no gravitational slip) with higher-order deviations bounded by |δγ| < 1e-19, and dual screening suppresses Solar System modifications 10^4–10^8 below the Cassini |γ − 1| bound.
datasets_used: SPARC galaxy rotation-curve fits (for g_dagger and rho_star calibration)

sealed_predictions.statement: All Solar System 1PN observables sensitive to gravitational slip will yield γ = 1 with no detectable deviation; any γ − 1 arises only beyond linear order and remains below 1e-19.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Next-generation Shapiro time-delay or light-deflection measurements during solar conjunctions (e.g., precision radio science, VLBI) that robustly detect γ − 1 above 1e-19.

kill_criteria: KC1: A robust Solar System detection of gravitational slip (Ψ ≠ Φ) at 1PN order, i.e., γ − 1 ≠ 0 inconsistent with zero within systematics.
KC2: A confirmed measurement of |γ − 1| ≥ 1e-7 in Solar System experiments (e.g., Shapiro delay, light deflection), contradicting the EFC bound |δγ| < 1e-19 from its scalar-rescaling structure.

KC3: Observation of spatial or density-correlated variation of the effective Newton's constant within the inner Solar System at levels incompatible with Θ(ρ_eff) ≈ 0 and μ(ĝ) ≈ 1 (i.e., unsuppressed modifications where the model predicts saturation).

KC4: Detection of composition-dependent free fall or a nonzero Nordtvedt parameter inconsistent with a universal scalar rescaling of GN at the current or improved LLR precision, attributable to metric-sector modifications.
abstract: Demonstrates EFC compatibility with Solar System precision tests through dual screening mechanisms. Derives γ = 1 from field equations with |δγ| < 10^-19 at higher order.
key_result: EFC modifications suppressed 10^4-10^8 below Cassini bound; γ = 1 derived as theorem

ppn_analysis.key_property: Scalar rescaling of G_N (not anisotropic coupling)

wep.mechanism: Universal coupling to T_μν (source-dependent, not test-body-dependent)

comparison_with_other_screening.chameleon: EFC advantage: No extra degree of freedom
comparison_with_other_screening.symmetron: EFC advantage: No spontaneous symmetry breaking needed
comparison_with_other_screening.vainshtein: EFC advantage: Algebraic screening, not kinetic

open_questions: Covariant action → field equation formal derivation
Formal SEP proof at all orders
